Front: What is the fundamental difference between SFT and RL for post-training?
Back: SFT minimizes distance to demonstration distribution (imitation); RL maximizes a reward signal (optimization). SFT is bounded by demo quality; RL can exceed it but introduces instability

Front: What is the "killer framing" for SFT vs RL?
Back: SFT teaches a model WHAT to say; RL teaches it HOW WELL to say it. SFT sets the floor; RL raises the ceiling — but only for properties the reward signal can capture

Front: What compute overhead does each RL method add beyond SFT?
Back: DPO: 1.5-2x; GRPO: 2-3x; online iterative DPO: 3-4x; PPO: 4-6x

Front: What are the 5 things RL unlocks that SFT cannot?
Back: Simultaneous accuracy+diversity; self-correction; emergent reasoning strategies; exploration beyond training data; holistic property optimization

Front: What is the Elicitation Theory of RL?
Back: RL does NOT teach new capabilities — it elicits and amplifies latent ones; base models at high pass@k solve everything RL models solve at pass@1

Front: What is the implication of the Elicitation Theory?
Back: If base model cannot solve a problem at all (even at pass@1000), RL will not help; invest in better pretraining or distillation for genuinely new capabilities

Front: Why is RL described as "offline best-of-N baked into the weights"?
Back: RL reshapes the distribution once during training so pass@1 is as good as pass@N was; this amortizes the N-times inference cost into a one-time training cost

Front: What did Singhal et al. show about RLHF improvements?
Back: RLHF improvements are "largely driven by increasing response length"; a purely length-based reward reproduces most gains; real RL value appears in safety and reasoning

Front: How do you test if your RLHF model just learned length bias?
Back: Compare against an SFT model with a "always be verbose" instruction; if they're similar, your reward model learned length not quality

Front: What did InstructGPT's 1.3B RLHF model prove?
Back: It was preferred over the 175B base GPT-3, proving RL adds qualitative value that scaling alone doesn't provide

Front: Why can't you just collect more demonstrations and skip RL?
Back: Ranking outputs is 10x cheaper than writing perfect ones; ranking captures holistic quality that's hard to specify in a demonstration; RL exploits this asymmetry between evaluation and generation

Front: Did DeepSeek-R1 invalidate the SFT then RL pipeline?
Back: No; R1-Zero (pure RL) works but is less efficient. R1 (SFT cold start + GRPO) outperforms. SFT makes RL more sample-efficient by reducing compute 2-5x

Front: What behaviors "emerged" from DeepSeek-R1's pure RL?
Back: Self-reflection, verification, and dynamic strategy switching — metacognitive behaviors not in any training data, arising because GRPO incentivized checking work

Front: How do you detect reward hacking?
Back: Monitor correlation between reward score and true quality (held-out human eval); when they diverge, model is hacking. Track length growth, human preference plateau, RM confidence

Front: What is Gao et al.'s inverted-U finding?
Back: Gold reward follows an inverted-U as proxy optimization increases; model initially improves genuinely then starts exploiting reward model blind spots

Front: Is there a theoretical limit to optimizing against a reward model?
Back: Yes — optimal KL budget depends on RM quality; with imperfect RM there's an optimal stopping point beyond which true quality degrades. Stop when held-out eval plateaus, not when reward plateaus

Front: How does SCoRe (Self-Correction via RL) compare to SFT for self-correction?
Back: SCoRe improves by 15.6% on MATH where SFT-based self-correction fails entirely

Front: What is PRIME and what did it achieve?
Back: Process RL with implicit rewards; 15.1% improvement over SFT using only 10% of training data

Front: What is TTRL and its result?
Back: Test-Time RL using majority voting as pseudo-rewards; achieved 211% improvement on AIME math competition problems

Front: What did SimPO achieve vs DPO?
Back: Reference-free DPO that outperforms standard DPO by 6.4 points on AlpacaEval 2

Front: When is RL worth the 1.5-6x compute cost?
Back: Quality gap > 3% between SFT and desired output; safety alignment needed; verifiable rewards exist (math, code); scale justifies fixed cost (millions of users)

Front: When is RL NOT worth the cost?
Back: SFT achieves acceptable quality; no reliable reward signal exists; budget allows <2x compute; task is simple format transfer

Front: What is the cost for SFT vs DPO vs GRPO vs PPO on 70B model?
What is the data cost difference between SFT and GRPO?
Back: SFT: $5-50 per expert demonstration, needs 10K-100K. GRPO: ~$0 marginal cost (prompts + verifiable rewards, unlimited)

Front: What gap size determines the right post-training method?
Back: Gap <3%: SFT sufficient. Gap 3-10%: add DPO. Gap >10% or safety-critical: full RL (PPO/GRPO)

Front: What is RFT (Reinforcement Fine-Tuning)?
Back: OpenAI product using RL with rubrics instead of demonstrations; minimal annotation (100s-1000s of rubrics at $0.10-1 each)

Front: What "Staff says" vs "Principal says" about DeepSeek?
Back: Staff: "DeepSeek did pure RL, we should too." Principal: "R1-Zero works but R1 (SFT+GRPO) is more efficient. Pure RL is a research result, not an operational recommendation"

Front: What "Staff says" vs "Principal says" about RLHF teaching reasoning?
Back: Staff: "RL teaches the model to reason." Principal: "RL redistributes probability mass onto correct solutions already latent. If pass@1000 can't solve it, RL won't either"

Front: What does the industry-standard post-training pipeline look like?
Back: Stage 1: SFT (expert demos, format+baseline, 1x compute); Stage 2: Reward signal (human/AI/verifiable); Stage 3: RL optimization (1.5-6x compute); Stage 4: Evaluation + regression checks

Front: What is the SFT ceiling problem?
Back: SFT is bounded by the quality of demonstrations; RL can exceed this ceiling but only for properties the reward signal can capture; RL with reward hacking can also degrade below the ceiling

Front: How do you prevent reward hacking?
Back: KL penalty, length normalization, diverse reward signals, process rewards over outcome rewards; stop when held-out eval plateaus

Front: What is the MoE SFT problem with LoRA targeting MLP layers?
Back: MLP/expert layers are sparse and don't interact well with PEFT; should target attention only (q/k/v/o projections)

Front: Why might 5K samples be insufficient for 128-expert MoE?
Back: Each expert gets ~3% of tokens, meaning only ~150 effective samples per expert; need 50K+ with task diversity

Front: What is the diagnostic for choosing distillation vs RL for MoE?
Back: pass@100 at T=0.8: High means use DPO (model knows but is inconsistent); Low means distill from teacher (50-100K CoT demos)

Front: What is Constitutional AI's approach to safety?
Back: Uses harmlessness without human harm labels via constitutional principles; enables safety alignment that SFT alone cannot achieve (SFT creates over/under-refusal)

Front: When does SFT alone work poorly for safety?
Back: SFT-only safety creates over-refusal or under-refusal; RL enables nuanced safety boundaries that generalize to adversarial inputs

Front: What does "SFT + online iterative RLHF" achieve?
Back: Highest quality but most complex; Self-Rewarding LLMs outperform GPT-4 through iterative self-improvement rounds

Front: What is Process Reward Model (PRM) and when to use it?
Back: Provides credit assignment in multi-step reasoning by scoring each step, not just the final answer; use for tasks where final answer alone gives insufficient signal

Front: What is the recommended pipeline for GPT-OSS-120B MoE?
Back: 1: Distill 50-100K demos from Claude/GPT-4 with CoT; 2: SFT with LoRA rank=64 attention-only LR=3e-4; 3: DPO with generated+verified preference pairs; 4: Deploy

Front: What models in memory does each RL method require?
Back: SFT: 1 model; DPO: 2 (policy + reference); GRPO: 1 + sampling; PPO: 4 (policy, reference, RM, value head)

Front: What does ESFT reveal about MoE expert usage per task?
Back: Routing is concentrated in 5-15% of experts per task; single-task data doesn't engage diverse expert routing

Front: What is the "Staff says" vs "Principal says" about SFT ceiling?
Back: Staff: "We need RLHF to improve our model." Principal: "First measure the SFT ceiling. If within 3% of target, DPO is sufficient at 1/4 the cost of PPO"

Front: What is the difference between distillation and RL for MoE?
Back: Distillation: instills new capability, CoT demos engage more experts, needs teacher model. RL (DPO/GRPO): improves consistency of existing capability, respects routing specialization
